questions.skill: Classify numbers as rational or irrational
questions.prompt: Is √50 rational or irrational? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup: Is √50 rational or irrational? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Irrational. 50 is not a perfect square, so √50 cannot be written as a quotient of integers; its decimal neither ends nor repeats.

sections.skill: Decide whether sums and products are rational or irrational

questions.domain: Number & Quantity: The Real Number System
questions.skill: Decide whether sums and products are rational or irrational
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Explain why 4 + √3 is irrational. (Suppose 4 + √3 = r for some rational number r, and see what that would say about √3.)
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why 4 + √3 is irrational. (Suppose 4 + √3 = r for some rational number r, and see what that would say about √3.)
questions.required_method: An argument like this: if 4 + √3 = r with r rational, then √3 = r - 4, a difference of two rational numbers, which is rational. But √3 is irrational, so 4 + √3 cannot be rational.
